title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 3 and 4.
This question paper consists of 7 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

questions.prompt: What is the $y$-intercept of $y = -2x + 7$?
questions.explanation: $c = 7$: the line cuts the $y$-axis at $(0;\ 7)$.

questions.prompt: The graph of $y = 4$ is a horizontal line.
questions.explanation: $y$ is always 4, whatever $x$ is: a horizontal line with gradient 0.

questions.prompt: Which line is parallel to $y = 2x + 1$?
questions.explanation: Parallel lines have the same gradient, $2$.

questions.prompt: A line with a negative gradient goes up from left to right.
questions.explanation: A negative gradient means $y$ decreases as $x$ increases: the line goes down from left to right.

questions.prompt: Find the equation of the straight line through $(1;\ 5)$ and $(3;\ 9)$.
Find, algebraically, the point of intersection of $y = 2x - 1$ and $y = -x + 2$.

sections.title: QUESTION 2: Perimeter, Area and the Theorem of Pythagoras

questions.prompt: Which formula gives the area of a trapezium with parallel sides $a$ and $b$ and height $h$?
questions.explanation: Half the sum of the parallel sides times the height.

questions.prompt: An isosceles trapezium has parallel sides of 14 cm and 8 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the length of each slanting side.
questions.explanation: Overhang $= 3$ cm; $\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5$ cm.

questions.prompt: Doubling the radius of a circle doubles its area.
questions.explanation: $\pi(2r)^2 = 4\pi r^2$: the area is multiplied by 4.

questions.prompt: Match each shape with its area formula.
questions.explanation: These formulae come from cutting and rearranging shapes into rectangles.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 5 cm wide and its diagonal is 13 cm. Calculate its area.
questions.explanation: Length $= \sqrt{169 - 25} = 12$ cm; area $= 5 \times 12 = 60\ \text{cm}^2$.

questions.prompt:
A kite has diagonals of 12 cm and 20 cm. The long diagonal bisects the short one, and is divided by it into parts of 8 cm and 12 cm.
(a) Calculate the area of the kite.  (1)
(b) Calculate the lengths of its sides, correct to two decimal places where necessary.  (3)
questions.memo:
(a) $\frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 20 = 120\ \text{cm}^2$ ✓ (1)
(b) Half of the short diagonal $= 6$ cm ✓ (1)
Short sides: $\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10$ cm ✓ (1)
Long sides: $\sqrt{6^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{180} \approx 13{,}42$ cm ✓ (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 3: Surface Area and Volume of 3D Objects

questions.prompt: Which expression gives the area of the curved surface of a cylinder?
questions.explanation: The curved surface unrolls into a rectangle $2\pi r$ by $h$.

questions.prompt: A cylindrical container has radius 10 cm and height 30 cm. How many litres does it hold? Round to two decimal places.
Doubling the radius of a cylinder (keeping the height the same) doubles its volume.
questions.explanation: $\pi(2r)^2h = 4\pi r^2h$: the volume is multiplied by 4.

questions.prompt: A cylinder has a volume of $500\ \text{cm}^3$ and a radius of 5 cm. Calculate its height, correct to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: $h = \frac{500}{\pi \times 25} \approx 6{,}37$ cm.

questions.prompt: Match each object with its volume formula.
questions.explanation: Each is (area of base) × height.

questions.prompt: Every dimension of a box is tripled. By what number is its volume multiplied?
A paper label covers the curved surface of a tin with diameter 8 cm and height 11 cm. Calculate the area of the label, correct to two decimal places.
Reflect $(2;\ -5)$ in the line $y = x$.
questions.explanation: Swap the coordinates: $(x;\ y) \to (y;\ x)$.

questions.prompt: A reflection in the line $y = x$ maps $(a;\ b)$ to $(b;\ a)$.
questions.explanation: The coordinates are swapped.

questions.prompt: Match each rule with the transformation it describes.

pairs.right: Reflection in the line y = x

questions.explanation: Test each rule with a point such as $(1;\ 2)$ and sketch it.

questions.prompt: $A(2;\ 5)$ is mapped to $A'(5;\ 2)$ and $B(-1;\ 3)$ is mapped to $B'(3;\ -1)$ by the same transformation. Describe it fully.
questions.memo:
The coordinates are swapped: $(x;\ y) \to (y;\ x)$ ✓ (1)
Reflection in the line $y = x$ ✓ (1)

questions.prompt: What does the net of a closed cylinder consist of?
questions.explanation: The two circular ends and the curved surface, which unrolls into a rectangle.

questions.prompt: A cylinder has 2 curved edges and no vertices.
questions.explanation: The two circular rims are edges where the flat faces meet the curved surface; there are no corners.

questions.prompt: How many faces does an octagonal prism have?
questions.explanation: $n + 2 = 8 + 2 = 10$: two octagons and eight rectangles.

questions.prompt: Match each solid with its description.

pairs.right: One curved surface, no edges or vertices
Two flat circles and one curved surface
One flat circle, one curved surface and an apex

questions.explanation: Describe solids by their faces (or surfaces), edges and vertices.

questions.prompt: Euler's formula $F + V - E = 2$ applies to a cylinder.
questions.explanation: Euler's formula is for polyhedra; a cylinder has curved surfaces and is not a polyhedron.

questions.prompt: A toy rocket is made of a cone fixed on top of a cylinder of the same radius. List the surfaces of the rocket that you can see.
questions.memo:
One flat circle at the bottom and the curved surface of the cylinder ✓ (1)
The curved surface of the cone, ending at the apex (the circle where they join is hidden) ✓ (1)

questions.explanation: Lower half $3;\ 5;\ 7;\ 8$: median $= \frac{5 + 7}{2} = 6$.

questions.prompt: An outlier affects the interquartile range much more than it affects the range.
questions.explanation: The range uses the extreme values, so an outlier changes it a lot. The IQR uses only the middle 50%, so it hardly changes.

questions.prompt: Which graph is best for investigating whether two numerical variables are related?
questions.explanation: A scatter plot shows each pair of values as a point.

questions.prompt: The 50th percentile is the same as the...
questions.explanation: Half the data lies below the median.

questions.prompt: In 15 matches a team scored 0 goals 3 times, 1 goal 5 times, 2 goals 4 times, 3 goals twice and 4 goals once. Calculate the mean number of goals per match, correct to two decimal places.

The ages of people at a party are $5;\ 6;\ 6;\ 7;\ 8;\ 9;\ 40$.
(a) Identify the outlier.  (1)
(b) Calculate the mean with and without the outlier.  (2)
(c) Which measure, the mean or the median, better describes a typical age? Explain.  (1)
questions.memo:
(a) $40$ ✓ (1)
(b) With: $81 \div 7 \approx 11{,}57$ ✓; without: $41 \div 6 \approx 6{,}83$ ✓ (2)
(c) The median ($7$), because the outlier pulls the mean up ✓ (1)

questions.prompt: Two dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 8? Type a fraction (e.g. 5/36) or a decimal correct to three decimal places.
For independent events $A$ and $B$, which is true?
questions.explanation: Multiply the probabilities of independent events.

questions.prompt: When one die is rolled, "rolling a 2" and "rolling a 5" are mutually exclusive events.
questions.explanation: One roll cannot show both a 2 and a 5.

questions.prompt: A fair coin has landed heads three times in a row, so the next toss is more likely to be tails.
questions.explanation: Tosses are independent: $P(\text{tails}) = \frac{1}{2}$ every time.

questions.prompt:
A coin is tossed twice.
(a) Draw a tree diagram or list all the outcomes.  (1)
(b) Find $P(\text{exactly one head})$.  (2)
questions.memo:
(a) HH, HT, TH, TT ✓ (1)
(b) HT and TH ✓; $\frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$ ✓ (2)

questions.prompt:
Two dice are rolled.
(a) Find $P(\text{a double})$.  (2)
(b) Find $P(\text{sum greater than } 9)$.  (2)
